title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Scripture never says we sinned in Adam; 'in Adam' ≠ imputation
pass_a_gloss: Placeus: Scripture never says we sinned in Adam. Nor does 'in Adam' talk force an imputation that makes his alien act ours. We die in Adam, yet his death is not imputed.
pass_b_english: PLAC. First, Scripture does not say that we sinned in Adam. Next, I do not see why that manner of speaking should signify imputation by which another's sin, namely Adam's, becomes or exists as ours. For we are said to die in Adam, and yet Adam's death is not imputed to us.
source_text: PLAC. Primum, non dicit Scriptura nos in Adamo peccasse. Deinde, non video cur illa locutio vim significet imputationem, qua peccatum alienum, nempe Adami, fiat aut existat nostrum. Dicimur enim mori in Adamo, nec tamen mors Adami nobis imputatur.

choices.choice: No 'we sinned in Adam' text; dying in Adam ≠ Adam's death imputed
